findings.title: Bad CODEMIE_MODEL aborts launch under --profile
findings.problem: With --profile and no --model, ConfigLoader drops the env model (config.ts:228-231), yet the launcher still validates process.env.CODEMIE_MODEL (AgentCLI.ts:253-256) and exits 1 on a bad value the config never uses.
findings.impact: Trigger is narrow: --profile plus an invalid CODEMIE_MODEL exported in the shell; workaround is unsetting the variable, and the message names CODEMIE_MODEL as the source. Reachability confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the abort is intended (spec validates the user-supplied env value); if not, skip the env check when options.profile is set and options.model is undefined.

findings.title: Compressed request bodies bypass the model guard
findings.problem: modelOf returns found:false when the first non-blank byte is not '{', so a request with Content-Encoding gzip/br (or a UTF-16 body) skips validation. The class comment says a request cannot dodge the check, which overstates this. The proxy does not decode request bodies anywhere, so the Claude normalizers are bypassed the same way.
findings.impact: Needs a client that compresses its request body; Claude clients do not by default, and a BOM-prefixed body fails JSON.parse anyway. The bad value reaches the upstream, which validates it itself.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the comment to the content-type claim it actually makes, or reject/decode requests carrying a content-encoding header.

findings.title: Duplicate model keys: guard and upstream may disagree
findings.problem: JSON.parse keeps the last duplicate model key, so a body with a bad first and valid last value passes the guard; an upstream parser that keeps the first would see the bad one.
findings.impact: Reachability unconfirmed, no trigger built: mainstream JSON parsers also keep the last key, and the normalizer parses the same way.
findings.recommendation: Accept as is, or document that the guard judges the value a standard JSON parser sees.
